title: Four 3-Second Crashes Wiped a Day of Lessons | vitalii.no
description:
On November 21st, four separate three-second AI service failures in a row emptied the entire wall-lesson queue generated for November 23rd. Each crash was treated exactly like a real rejected attempt, burning one of a step's limited tries — so a handful of flaky API blips could wipe out a full day of lesson generation before a single real attempt ever ran.

I rebuilt the wall-lesson pipeline (scripts/home-pc/lessons/lessons_run.py) around a planner, editor and teacher split: two AI review passes run together on every open step, capped at two rounds, and a plan still unapproved by round two never reaches the builder stage — the old version only brought in a stricter check on a step's very last try. A dedicated teacher pass now records notes after fact-checking without ever issuing its own pass or fail verdict. Crucially, a crash or a failed API call no longer spends one of a step's limited tries — only a real, finished attempt does — and the working directory now survives a locked leftover folder from a previous crashed run instead of blocking the next attempt.

New nightly defaults cap each run at 400, 200 and 120 attempts inside a 00:30-07:00 window. The exact failure mode that erased a whole day of lessons — four three-second crashes in a row — can no longer happen.
